choices: Always a complete binary heap shape
items.whyRight: Connected + no cycles is the graph definition of a tree.
whyWrong: A cycle would make it not a tree.

items.prompt: Inorder traversal of a binary search tree yields keys in?
items.whyRight: Left → node → right respects BST order.
whyWrong: Insertion order is not what inorder guarantees.

items.prompt: Preorder is often chosen when you need to?
choices: Copy or serialize a tree shape root-first
items.whyRight: Root before children reconstructs structure easily.
whyWrong: Shortest unweighted paths are BFS on graphs.

items.prompt: Height of a skewed chain of n nodes is?
items.whyRight: Each level has one node; height tracks n.
whyWrong: Constant height cannot hold n nodes in a binary tree.
Square root is not the skew bound.
A stack alone yields DFS order.
Union-find merges sets, not tree levels.
Heaps order by priority, not discovery layer.

items.prompt: Postorder is the natural fit when each node’s value depends on?
choices: A global hash of all keys
items.whyRight: Children first, then combine at the node.
whyWrong: Parent-only dependency would not need child results.
A global hash is unrelated to traversal choice.
